offers_products.reason: Sells access to Dice and ClearanceJobs online talent marketplaces: job-posting and recruiter database subscriptions, which are software/SaaS.

offers_services.reason: Revenue is mainly platform subscriptions; adjacent services are only mentioned as an extension, not a main offering.

sells_to_consumers.reason: Employers and recruiters pay; candidates use the platforms free as job seekers and are not the main buyers.

sells_to_organizations.reason: Employers, recruiters and defense contractors like Lockheed Martin, Booz Allen and Leidos buy recruiting subscriptions.

recurring_revenue.reason: Recruiter subscriptions and package contracts on Dice and ClearanceJobs renew repeatedly, with ongoing repeat employer purchases.

cyclical_demand.reason: Employers cut recruiting and tech hiring spend in downturns, so job-posting subscriptions are easily reduced.

big_ticket.reason: Subscriptions and job-posting packages are small, recurring purchases relative to employers' budgets.

people_delivered.reason: Customers pay for access to online marketplaces, candidate databases and matching technology, not staff time.

large_customers.reason: Customers include large defense contractors, but also many recruiters and smaller employers on Dice; mix is unclear.

asset_heavy.reason: Online platforms and software need little physical investment in plants, fleets or properties.

notes: Customer size mix is uncertain; website names large defense contractors but also general recruiters.
